item.title: VIctory says GTA VI menus reach 30 FPS and the world loads, but the port is not playable
item.description: Marvisak's VIctory project reports GTA VI Xbox Series code booting on Windows, menus at 30 FPS and loading into the world. Its README says the world rendering is still broken, frames can take seconds, and the software is not playable. These are developer statements, not independently reproduced tests. Why it matters: An initial boot and world loading are not playable gameplay. VIctory's README warns that the world-rendering path may hang a real GPU and reset the Windows display driver. Do not treat the project or a claimed build as independently cleared for safety.

item.title: VIctory developer reports GTA VI menus and partial world startup; not playable
item.description: VIctory is a new Rust-based attempt to run the Xbox Series GTA VI build on Windows. Its November 23 README reports 30 FPS menus, an intro video and reaching early world-loading stages; world rendering is incomplete and slow. The author explicitly says the project is not playable yet. These are developer-reported results, not independently reproduced tests. Why it matters: The project represents a concrete research effort with public source code, but its README also warns that real-GPU world loading can crash the display driver. Neither source visibility nor self-reported footage proves a safe, working PC port.
